Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
Would it be possible to disable rendering the [ pre ] tag on the forum? It breaks people who are copying card text that includes a Presence level. Example: www.vekn.net/forum/rules-questions/72635-dam-the-heart-s-river-and-catatonic-fear

As far as I know, it worked the right way (for V:TES) on the old forum, so I'm assuming there's a setting somewhere that can be tweaked/modified/overridden.

Messages.Author: Damnans
Messages.Body:
I can't seem to find the way to do it.

If anyone does, please let me know.

V:EKN Website Coordinator

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
I don't know what the best way to do this is, but looking at the most recent code on www.kunena.org/ there's a file called "bbcode.php" which maps each of the tags to the corresponding html. There's this: 'pre' => array( 'simple_start' => "
",
'simple_end' => "
", 'class' => 'block', 'allow_in' => array('listitem', 'block', 'columns'), 'plain_start' => "", 'plain_end' => "", ), Which appears to be the code which controls that [ pre ] goes to 
. I suspect that commenting it all out (preceding each line with //) or deleting it would do the trick.

With the current code, it would probably look a bit like:

...
'tt' => array(
'simple_start' => "",
'simple_end' => "",
'class' => 'inline',
'allow_in' => array('listitem', 'block', 'columns', 'inline', 'link'),
'plain_start' => "",
'plain_end' => "",
),

// 'pre' => array(
// 'simple_start' => "
",
// 'simple_end' => "
",
// 'class' => 'block',
// 'allow_in' => array('listitem', 'block', 'columns'),
// 'plain_start' => "",
// 'plain_end' => "",
// ),

'font' => array(
'mode' => BBCODE_MODE_LIBRARY,
'allow' => array('_default' => '/^[a-zA-Z0-9._ -]+$/'),
'method' => 'DoFont',
'class' => 'inline',
'allow_in' => array('listitem', 'block', 'columns', 'inline', 'link'),
),
...

Or possibly just changing the "pre" to something else, like "preformat":

'preformat' => array(
'simple_start' => "
",
'simple_end' => "
",
'class' => 'block',
'allow_in' => array('listitem', 'block', 'columns'),
'plain_start' => "",
'plain_end' => "",
),

Disclaimer: completely untested.
